# PropertyIQ

> AI-powered real estate market intelligence platform that ranks 900+ US metros, 3,000+ counties, and 29,000+ ZIP codes.

_Last updated: 2026-07-09_

## Overview

PropertyIQ generates a single PropertyIQ Score (1-99) that predicts a market's 3-year performance relative to its state. The score is built from four monthly market signals — Zillow home-value momentum (12-month and 3-month) plus Realtor.com median days on market and the share of listings with price cuts. It is a transparent, equal-weight formula with no fitted parameters or black-box model. Validated across 20+ years of out-of-sample data (2001-2023 scoring vintages), the score-to-return relationship is positive in every backtested year at every geography level.

## Scoring System

PropertyIQ generates a single **PropertyIQ Score** (1-99) for every geography:

- **50 = state average** — higher predicts outperformance relative to the market's state over the next 3 years
- Built from 4 demand-signal inputs: Zillow ZHVI 12-month momentum (positive), Zillow ZHVI 3-month momentum (positive), Realtor.com median days on market (negative), and the share of listings with price cuts (negative)
- Formula: `z(zhvi_yoy) + z(zhvi_mom_3m) − z(median_days_on_market) − z(price_reduced_share)`, equal weights, no fitted parameters
- Each input is converted to a cross-sectional z-score across all markets at a geography level each month (national basis), summed, percentile-ranked, re-centered so the zero-crossing maps to 50, and clamped 1-99
- Coverage: 900+ metros, 3,000+ counties, 29,000+ ZIPs; monthly history backfilled to 2001

### Validation Results

Validated out-of-sample across 2001-2023 scoring vintages (20+ years, two full housing cycles):
- The score-to-return relationship is positive in every validated calendar year at metro, county, and ZIP levels
- 2016-onward out-of-sample information coefficient (3-year forward excess return vs state): +0.27 metro, +0.20 county, +0.20 ZIP
- Monotonic score-band separation: higher score bands realize higher 3-year excess returns vs state with no adjacent inversions
- Permutation tests place the signal far above a shuffled-target null at every geography level

## Detailed Methodology

### PropertyIQ Score Formula

The PropertyIQ Score predicts a market's 3-year excess return relative to its state, built from four monthly demand-signal inputs:

1. Four inputs are collected: Zillow ZHVI 12-month price momentum (positive signal), Zillow ZHVI 3-month price momentum (positive signal), Realtor.com median days on market (negative signal), and the share of listings with price cuts (negative signal). The two momentum inputs come from Zillow; the two flow inputs come from Realtor.com. No Redfin data is used in the score.
2. Each input is converted to a cross-sectional z-score across all markets at the same geography level for that month — a national basis, not partitioned by state.
3. The signal is computed as: `z(zhvi_yoy) + z(zhvi_mom_3m) − z(median_days_on_market) − z(price_reduced_share)`, with equal weights and no fitted parameters.
4. The raw signal is converted to a cross-sectional percentile rank, re-centered so the zero-crossing maps to 50 at every geography level, and clamped to the 1-99 range.
5. A score of 50 corresponds to the state average. The scale is calibrated and empirically validated so that 50 equals a market's state-average 3-year performance: higher scores predict outperformance, and lower scores predict underperformance, relative to the market's own state. (The computation is national-basis; the prediction target is within-state.)

This formula is transparent, reproducible, and uses only observable market signals. There is no black-box ML model — the score is a direct, equal-weight function of measurable market conditions. Engine requires at least 2 of the 4 inputs; a per-score A/B/C/F confidence grade reflects how many inputs were available and fresh, independent of the score value.

### Walk-Forward Validation Process

The PropertyIQ Score has been validated out-of-sample across 2001-2023 scoring vintages (20+ years spanning two full housing cycles). For each scoring date, the score is computed using only data available at that time, then evaluated against actual home price changes (Zillow ZHVI) over the subsequent 3-year period. All results are out-of-sample in time.

Key validation results:
- The score-to-return relationship is positive in every validated calendar year at metro, county, and ZIP levels.
- 2016-onward out-of-sample information coefficient (per-month Spearman correlation of score vs 3-year forward excess-vs-state return): approximately +0.27 metro, +0.20 county, +0.20 ZIP. The signal is strongest from 2016 onward, when all four inputs are present; pre-2016 vintages use price momentum only and carry lower confidence.
- Monotonic score-band separation: average 3-year excess returns vs state increase consistently from the lowest score band to the highest, with no adjacent inversions.
- Permutation tests place the signal many standard deviations above a shuffled-target null at every geography level.

### Data Sources

The score uses Zillow ZHVI for its two price-momentum inputs and Realtor.com for its two listing-flow inputs (median days on market and price-cut share). Missing values are handled through the MetricResolutionService's geographic inheritance system, which walks up the geography hierarchy (ZIP to county to metro to state) when primary data is unavailable.

Scores are recomputed monthly as new data arrives. Coverage spans 900+ metros, 3,000+ counties, and 29,000+ ZIP codes, with monthly history backfilled to 2001.
